column1: What are the four most-tested dimensions of responsible AI?
column2: Fairness, explainability, privacy and security, and transparency.

column1: Fairness — key question and primary AWS tool?
column2: Equitable treatment across groups/protected characteristics?; SageMaker Clarify (bias metrics).

column1: Explainability — key question and primary AWS tool?
column2: Why did the model produce this prediction?; SageMaker Clarify (SHAP).

column1: Privacy and security — key question and primary AWS tool?
column2: Is personal data protected; is the model protected from misuse?; Guardrails (PII redaction); Amazon Macie.

column1: Transparency — key question and primary AWS tool?
column2: Is the whole system's build/training/limits documented?; SageMaker Model Cards / AI Service Cards.

column1: Veracity and robustness — key question and primary AWS tool?
column2: Correct and reliable, even under noisy/adversarial input?; Guardrails (contextual grounding).

column1: Governance — key question and primary AWS tool?
column2: Policies/processes controlling the AI lifecycle?; Model Cards; ML lineage tracking.

column1: Safety — key question and primary AWS tool?
column2: Avoids harmful/dangerous generated content?; Guardrails (content filters).

column1: Controllability — key question and primary AWS tool?
column2: Can a human monitor, override, or stop it?; Guardrails (denied topics); Amazon A2I.

column1: One prediction vs. the whole system documented — explainability or transparency?
column2: One prediction → explainability; whole system documented → transparency.

column1: Sampling bias — definition?
column2: Training data doesn't represent the real-world population.

column1: Measurement bias — definition?
column2: A proxy feature (e.g., ZIP code) correlates with a protected characteristic more than the real outcome.

column1: Label / human bias — definition?
column2: Annotators inject conscious/unconscious bias while labeling.

column1: Historical bias — definition?
column2: Data accurately reflects a real world that is itself inequitable.

column1: Exclusion bias — definition?
column2: Relevant data/features dropped, removing signal a group needs.

column1: Aggregation bias — definition?
column2: One model applied uniformly to groups that need distinct treatment.

column1: Representativeness bias — definition?
column2: A whole deployment segment (region/market) is thin/absent from training data — no group label exists, so standard fairness metrics miss it.

column1: A named proxy variable in a scenario points to which bias, and how is it fixed?
column2: Measurement bias — fixed by dropping/transforming the feature, not by rebalancing classes.

column1: Does a clean fairness-metric report rule out representativeness bias?
column2: No — check per-segment coverage and accuracy separately.

column1: Positive label rate differs across groups in the dataset — which metric, stage?
column2: Difference in proportions of labels (DPL); pre-training (Clarify dataset job).

column1: A class/group is underrepresented in the dataset — which metric, stage?
column2: Class imbalance; pre-training (Clarify dataset job).

column1: A trained model's outcome rates differ across groups — which metric, stage?
column2: Disparate impact; post-training (Clarify model job).

column1: Accuracy/recall differs materially across groups — which metric, stage?
column2: Accuracy/recall difference; post-training (Clarify model job).

column1: Credit/loan approval — highest-value fairness metric?
column2: Disparate impact + DPL (pre- and post-training).

column1: Healthcare triage/diagnosis — highest-value fairness metric?
column2: Accuracy/recall difference across demographic groups.

column1: RAG/generative assistant — what should you audit instead of a labeled-dataset fairness metric?
column2: The retrieval corpus's coverage (no labeled dataset exists).

column1: No model yet, checking labels vs. predictions from a deployed model — which metric family applies?
column2: No model yet → DPL/class imbalance; predictions/deployed model → disparate impact/accuracy-recall difference.

column1: Fairness vs. accuracy — typical fix to favor fairness?
column2: Pre-processing rebalance, in-processing fairness constraints, post-processing threshold calibration.

column1: Fairness vs. accuracy — when do you favor fairness over accuracy?
column2: High-stakes, regulated decisions (credit, hiring, healthcare).

column1: Natively interpretable model vs. post-hoc SHAP — added inference-time compute?
column2: Natively interpretable: none, the model's logic is the explanation. Post-hoc SHAP: extra computation per explanation, often run offline/batch.

column1: Does post-hoc SHAP reflect the model's actual decision logic?
column2: No — it's an approximation only; a natively interpretable model is required if the regulation demands actual decision logic.

column1: Explanation required AND strict real-time latency — which model type?
column2: A natively interpretable model, not synchronous post-hoc SHAP.

column1: Amazon SageMaker Clarify — primary use case?
column2: Bias detection (pre-/post-training) + SHAP explainability, on datasets and trained models.

column1: SageMaker Model Cards — what do they document?
column2: Structured documentation of a model you built.

column1: AI Service Cards — what do they document, and who authors them?
column2: AWS-published documentation of an AWS-managed AI service — AWS authors it, you read it.

column1: Model Card vs. AI Service Card — who fills it in?
column2: Model Card = you fill it in (a model you built); AI Service Card = AWS publishes it (an AWS-managed service).

column1: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock — primary use case?
column2: Runtime safety/privacy filtering on FM inputs/outputs at inference.

column1: Amazon A2I — primary use case?
column2: Human-in-the-loop review of low-confidence/high-stakes ML/AWS AI service predictions.

column1: Guardrails denied topics capability?
column2: Blocks the model from engaging with specified topics.

column1: Guardrails content filters capability?
column2: Blocks harmful categories (hate, insults, sexual, violence, misconduct, prompt attacks).

column1: Guardrails word filters capability?
column2: Blocks specific words/phrases (profanity, competitor names).

column1: Guardrails sensitive information filters capability?
column2: Detects/redacts/blocks PII in prompts and responses.

column1: Guardrails contextual grounding checks capability?
column2: Verifies a response is grounded in source content, reducing hallucination.

column1: Amazon A2I — what triggers StartHumanLoop?
column2: A prediction below the routing confidence threshold.

column1: Amazon A2I flow definition — what must match the routing logic?
column2: The activation condition must use the same threshold as the routing logic so the two never drift apart.

column1: When is a private workforce (via Amazon Cognito) required for Amazon A2I review instead of public Mechanical Turk?
column2: Whenever the review task exposes regulated data (e.g., PHI).

column1: SageMaker Clarify pre-training bias metrics?
column2: Class imbalance, difference in proportions of labels (DPL), computed on the raw dataset.

column1: SageMaker Clarify post-training bias metrics?
column2: Disparate impact, accuracy/recall difference, computed on a trained model's predictions.

column1: What does SageMaker Clarify integrate with for ongoing bias-drift monitoring?
column2: SageMaker Model Monitor.

column1: Does SageMaker Clarify apply to live foundation-model input/output?
column2: No — it applies to datasets and trained models (typically SageMaker); Guardrails covers live FM input/output.

column1: Intellectual property (IP) risk — what covers it, and AWS mitigation?
column2: Ownership of AI-generated content / liability for content resembling copyrighted training material; choose a Bedrock provider offering IP indemnification.

column1: Data privacy — what does it cover, and AWS mitigation?
column2: GDPR, data residency, minimizing/anonymizing personal data; Guardrails sensitive information filters (PII redaction); Amazon Macie.

column1: Toxicity — what does it cover, and AWS mitigation?
column2: Hateful, harassing, obscene, or otherwise harmful generated content; Guardrails content filters; Amazon A2I human review.

column1: Environmental impact — what does it cover, and AWS mitigation?
column2: Energy/compute/carbon footprint of training and running FMs; reuse pretrained FMs, AWS Customer Carbon Footprint Tool, Well-Architected Sustainability Pillar.

column1: IP risk — Guardrails or IP indemnification?
column2: IP indemnification — Guardrails covers content safety/privacy, not copyright liability.

column1: Bias drift — how is it tracked?
column2: Disparate impact / accuracy-recall difference tracked over time via SageMaker Model Monitor + Clarify.

column1: Confidence-threshold drift — what does it signal?
column2: A rising share of predictions below an Amazon A2I routing threshold signals population drift.

column1: Two-component systems (a structured model + a paired FM) — how should they be monitored?
column2: Each gets its own independent monitoring stream, never one blended metric.

column1: Governance cadence — what's the recommended recurring review?
column2: A recurring (e.g. quarterly) review of the SageMaker Model Card against the latest Clarify/Model Monitor metrics; high-risk flags route through Amazon A2I.

column1: Responsible AI
column2: Fair, explainable, private/secure, transparent, veracious/robust, governed, safe, and controllable AI systems.

column1: SHAP
column2: Feature-attribution values quantifying one prediction; an approximation, not an exact decision trace.

column1: PII
column2: Personally identifiable information; a Guardrails sensitive-information-filter target.

column1: IP indemnification
column2: A contractual protection shifting IP-infringement legal risk away from the customer.

column1: AWS Customer Carbon Footprint Tool
column2: Reports estimated carbon emissions from a customer's AWS usage.

column1: Amazon Macie
column2: Discovers/classifies sensitive data (incl. PII) stored in Amazon S3.

column1: Bias vs. variance — how do these differ?
column2: Bias (fairness) is a training-data/equity problem; variance (Domain 1) is a model-sensitivity/overfitting problem — don't conflate them.

column1: Guardrails vs. Clarify — what does each NOT do?
column2: Guardrails filters live inference content but doesn't detect training-data bias or generate explanations; that's Clarify's job.

column1: A pipeline with a tabular model plus a generative FM — which tool covers which component?
column2: SageMaker Clarify on the tabular model, Guardrails on the FM — never one blended tool/metric.
